newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian banks against minimum reserve requirements.
newsitem.headline: Belgian banks against minimum reserve requirements.

text.p: Belgian banks are opposed to the introduction of the technique of minimum reserve requirements for banks as an instrument of monetary policy when the European single currency comes into force in 1999, they said on Wednesday.

"We hope our Belgian central bank governor can convince the Bundesbank that there are other, and probably better, instruments of monetary policy than minimum reserve requirements and that in any case such reserves should earn interest at market rates," said Willy Breesch, new director of the Belgian Banking Association (BBA).
Breesch, who succeeds Ferdinand Chaffart, is chief executive officer of Belgium's Cera Bank.

The Belgian central bank does not impose minimum reserve requirements, unlike the Bundesbank. The latter obliges German banks to hold between 1.5 and two percent of the short-term money they borrow from foreign banks and domestic non-banks in non-interest bearing deposits at the Bundesbank.
The European banking industry is worried that the future European Central Bank will also adopt minimum reserve requirements as a tool for monetary policy as of 1999.
-- Geert De Clercq, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6813, Fax +32 2 230 7710
